findings.title: Missing administrator check for invitation creation
findings.description: Route allows any team member with a membership record to create an invite. This permits non-admin members to create invitations, violating REQ-AUTH-1.

findings.title: Export button labels queued exports as ready without ensuring downloadable file exists
findings.description: The new exportData function POSTs to /api/export and immediately shows a success toast: "Your export is ready to download". This labels the queued export as ready/downloadable before verifying a downloadable file exists (e.g., before polling or checking for file availability). This violates REQ-UX-3 which requires queued exports be labeled as processing until a downloadable file exists.

findings.title: Missing immutable audit event for manual invoice void
findings.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id. The new route handler calls voidInvoice(...) but does not create or record any audit event (no write to an audit log, database table, or append-only store). There is no code to persist an immutable record of the actor and invoice id or to include that information in the response. This is a concrete violation of REQ-AUDIT-1.

findings.title: Retry attempted regardless of 'cancelled' status
findings.description: Code increments attempts and calls send(notification) for any notification that exists and is not 'sent'. There is no check to prevent retries for notifications whose status is 'cancelled'. This violates REQ-NOTIFY-3 which requires that cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.

findings.title: Missing explicit check to allow retries only for 'pending' status
findings.description: The code only checks for 'sent' status and otherwise proceeds to retry. It does not verify the notification is in 'pending' state before incrementing attempts and sending, permitting retries for states other than pending (including cancelled). This directly contradicts REQ-NOTIFY-3.

findings.title: Sends billing reminders without checking opt-out preference
findings.description: The new reminders.ts unconditionally retrieves the user and sends an email reminder. findings.title: Display name length check counts all characters including whitespace
findings.description: REQ-VALID-1 requires the display name to contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters. The added code only checks displayName.length (total characters), so a string of two characters that are both whitespace (e.g., "  ") or a string with many whitespace characters could incorrectly pass or fail. The code does not ensure the count excludes whitespace characters or that there are at least 2 non-whitespace characters.

findings.title: No trimming or validation of internal/external whitespace
findings.description: The code neither trims nor removes whitespace before validation. For example, a displayName of " a" or "a " would be validated based on length including the space, which can allow names with fewer than 2 non-whitespace characters to pass or disallow otherwise valid names depending on surrounding spaces. REQ-VALID-1 mandates counting non-whitespace characters, but this logic is missing.

The new void route calls voidInvoice(...) and returns the invoice, but there is no code to create or persist an audit event (e.g., no call to an audit logging service, database insert, or append-only log).

findings.title: No audit event content verified to include actor and invoice id
findings.description: Even if the voidInvoice function creates an audit event internally, the route does not ensure or demonstrate that an immutable audit event containing both the actor and invoice id is recorded. There is no explicit construction or logging of an audit record including actor.id and params.invoiceId (or returned invoice.id).

findings.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried
findings.description: The code increments attempts and calls send() unconditionally when the notification exists and is not 'sent'. It only skips sending if status === 'sent', but does not check for status === 'cancelled'. Thus cancelled notifications would be retried/delivered, violating REQ-NOTIFY-3 which requires cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried.

findings.title: Sending billing reminders without respecting opt-out

findings.title: Queued exports labeled as ready before downloadable file exists
findings.description: The requirement REQ-UX-3 specifies: "The dashboard must label queued exports as processing until a downloadable file exists." The patch's exportData function sends a POST to start an export and immediately calls toast.success("Your export is ready to download"). This labels the export as ready/downloadable even though the server-side file may not yet exist (the POST merely queues/export creation). There is no check, poll, or confirmation that a downloadable file is available before signaling readiness.

It does not check for status === "cancelled" (or equivalent). As a result, cancelled notifications could be retried and delivered, violating REQ-NOTIFY-3: "Cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried."

benchmarkCase.title: Opted-out users receive billing notices
benchmarkCase.description: The sender omits notification preferences.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-4: Users opted out of non-essential billing reminders must not receive them.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A billing reminder is sent without reading the opt-out preference.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: The product disregards a user's communication choice.

expectedFindings.title: Billing reminder ignores opt-out preference
expectedFindings.description: The sender delivers a non-essential reminder without a preference check.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The sender must not send to a missing user.

findings.title: Sends billing reminders without checking opt-out preference
findings.description: The new code fetches a user and sends a reminder email unconditionally: it calls buildReminder(user) and sendEmail(user.email, message) for every user. It does not check whether the user has opted out of non-essential billing reminders, so users who have opted out would still receive them, violating REQ-NOTIFY-4.

benchmarkCase.title: Blank display names are accepted
benchmarkCase.description: Whitespace-only profile names pass length validation.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-VALID-1: A display name must contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint checks raw string length instead of trimmed content.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Profiles can have unusable blank identities.

expectedFindings.title: Display name lacks trimmed validation
expectedFindings.description: Whitespace-only names pass the length check.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Rejecting invalid types satisfies the API contract.

findings.title: Validation accepts whitespace-only names
findings.description: REQ-VALID-1 requires a display name to contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters. The new code only checks displayName.length, which counts all characters including whitespace. A name like "  " (two spaces) would pass the length check but contains zero non-whitespace characters, violating the requirement.

findings.title: No trimming or non-whitespace character check before saving
findings.description: The patch does not trim the displayName or verify the count of non-whitespace characters before calling saveProfile. This allows strings with leading/trailing spaces or strings that meet length bounds but have fewer than 2 non-whitespace characters to be persisted, violating REQ-VALID-1.

benchmarkCase.title: Role update regresses last-admin safeguard
benchmarkCase.description: The new role update path can demote the final administrator.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-REGRESS-1: A team must retain at least one administrator; role updates that would demote the final admin must be rejected.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The role update writes the requested role without checking remaining administrators.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: A team can become permanently unmanaged.

expectedFindings.title: Role change can demote the final administrator
expectedFindings.description: The update lacks the required last-admin safety check.

distractors.description: The target membership is checked for existence.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Rejecting an unknown membership is required input handling.

findings.title: No check to prevent demoting the final administrator
findings.description: The code simply sets member.role = role and saves without verifying whether this change would remove the last remaining administrator from the team. This violates REQ-REGRESS-1 which mandates that role updates that would demote the final admin must be rejected.

benchmarkCase.title: Starter plan seat limit is bypassed
benchmarkCase.description: The invitation flow omits the plan seat check.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-PLAN-2: Starter teams may have at most three active members; over-limit invitations must be rejected.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: An invitation is created without checking active seats against the Starter limit.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Customers can receive paid capacity without upgrading.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation ignores Starter seat limit
expectedFindings.description: The flow sends an invitation without checking the team's active seat count.

distractors.description: The email is checked for an at sign.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Basic email validation is independent of capacity enforcement.

findings.title: Does not enforce starter-team member limit
findings.description: REQ-PLAN-2 requires starter teams to have at most three active members and to reject invitations that would exceed that limit. The new inviteToTeam function does not check the team's plan/type or count of active members before creating an invitation. It unconditionally creates and sends an invitation, allowing invitations to be issued that could exceed the three-member limit for starter teams.

findings.title: No rejection of over-limit invitations
findings.description: REQ-PLAN-2 requires that over-limit invitations must be rejected. The function never rejects invitations based on member count; it only validates team existence and email format, then creates the invitation. There is no logic to reject or throw an error when an invitation would cause a starter team to exceed three active members.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled trial can be reactivated
benchmarkCase.description: The retry handler treats cancelled subscriptions as recoverable.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-STATE-2: A cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: Every non-active subscription is set to active.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: A user can be restored to a service they explicitly cancelled.

expectedFindings.title: Retry reactivates cancelled trials
expectedFindings.description: The handler changes cancelled trials to active.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Avoiding a redundant write is correct.

findings.title: Reactivating a cancelled trial by retry
findings.description: Code sets subscription.status = "active" and saves it for any subscription that exists but is not currently "active", which will reactivate subscriptions that were previously cancelled. This violates REQ-STATE-2 which requires a cancelled trial remain cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry.

findings.title: Invitations can be created by any team member with a membership record
findings.description: The new route handler checks only for existence of a membership record (findMembership) and returns 403 if none. It does not verify the membership role/administrative status (e.g., team administrator). As a result, any user who is a member of the team (not necessarily an administrator) can call createInvite and create invitations, violating REQ-AUTH-1 which states that only team administrators may create invitations.

findings.title: Missing immutable audit event when voiding invoices
findings.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id. The introduced route handler calls voidInvoice(params.invoiceId, actor.id) but does not record or emit any audit event after the void operation. There is no code creating an audit record (e.g., writing to an audit log, emitting an event, or calling an audit service) that includes the actor and invoice id. If voidInvoice does not itself create an immutable audit event, this change violates REQ-AUDIT-1.

decisions.explanation: The patched code enforces displayName length using string.length, which treats whitespace-only names as having length and therefore accepts them if length between 2 and 80. The requirement expects whitespace-only names to pass the length check (i.e., whitespace-only names are accepted). However, the contract title says 'Blank display names are accepted' and the criterion description 'Whitespace-only names pass the length check.' The code does not trim or check for non-whitespace characters, so whitespace-only names do pass — this behavior matches the criterion. benchmarkCase.title: Blank display names are accepted
benchmarkCase.description: Whitespace-only profile names pass length validation.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-VALID-1: A display name must contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint checks raw string length instead of trimmed content.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Profiles can have unusable blank identities.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Rejecting invalid types satisfies the API contract.

findings.title: blank-display-name
findings.description: The new route checks only the string length of displayName, allowing whitespace-only names to pass because it does not trim or validate non-whitespace characters. The criterion expects that whitespace-only names pass the length check (i.e., that the system accepts blank/whitespace-only display names). In context of the contract title 'Blank display names are accepted', the implemented checks do not reject whitespace-only names, so the requirement that whitespace-only names pass length check is satisfied by the code; however the contract wording indicates acceptance — to be explicit: the criterion is about whether whitespace-only names pass the length check. The code only enforces length and not non-whitespace character count, therefore whitespace-only names of length 2–80 will be accepted. If the intent of the criterion is that whitespace-only names should be accepted, the code satisfies it; but the contract requires that display name must contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters. Because the code fails to enforce 'non-whitespace characters' (it only enforces length), it violates the stated requirement that names must contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters.

reviewers.title: Display name validation allows whitespace-only names

Validate by trimming or ensuring at least two non-whitespace characters (e.g., using displayName.trim().length or a regex) before accepting the value.

reviewers.title: Role update allows demoting the last administrator

reviewers.title: Invitations do not enforce starter team member limit (REQ-PLAN-2)
reviewers.description: The inviteToTeam function creates and sends an invitation without checking the number of active members in the team. REQ-PLAN-2 requires that starter teams may have at most three active members and that invitations exceeding this limit must be rejected. The patch only retrieves the team, validates the email, creates an invitation, and sends email; it lacks any check of current active member count or logic to reject over-limit invitations.

reviewers.title: Starter team size limit not enforced for invitations

The new inviteToTeam function does not check the current number of active team members or enforce the three-member limit before creating an invitation. As a result, invitations that would cause a starter team to exceed three active members will be created and sent, violating the requirement.

reviewers.title: Cancelled subscription may be reactivated by retry
reviewers.description: The new code unconditionally sets subscription.status = "active" for any existing subscription that is not already "active". It retrieves a subscription and, if found and not active, immediately flips its status to active and saves. This allows a subscription with status "cancelled" to be reactivated by calling this code (e.g., via retry), violating REQ-STATE-2 which states a cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated.

reviewers.title: Cancelled subscription may be reactivated by retry

This allows previously cancelled trials to be reactivated by retry, violating REQ-STATE-2 which requires a cancelled trial remain cancelled and not be reactivated.

reviewers.title: Cancelled trial can be reactivated by retry

reviewers.title: Cancelled subscription may be reactivated by retry
reviewers.description: The new code loads a subscription and, if its status is anything other than "active", unconditionally sets subscription.status = "active" and saves it. That will flip a subscription whose status is "cancelled" back to "active" (for example if the operation is retried), violating REQ-STATE-2 which requires a cancelled trial remain cancelled and may not be reactivated.

benchmarkCase.title: Member can create team invitations
benchmarkCase.description: Membership is checked but the administrator role is omitted.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUTH-1: Only team administrators may create invitations.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The POST route permits any team member to create an invitation.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Regular members can expand a team without authorization.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation creation does not require an administrator
expectedFindings.description: A regular member can create an invitation because membership is checked without validating the admin role.

distractors.description: The route uses a generic unauthorized error.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: A non-enumerating error message is intentional.

findings.title: Missing admin check when creating team invitations
findings.description: The new route handler only verifies that the requester is a team member via findMembership(teamId, user.id) and returns 403 if not a member. It does not verify that the membership includes administrator privileges before calling createInvite, allowing non-admin members to create invitations. This is a direct violation of REQ-AUTH-1, which mandates that only team administrators may create invitations.

benchmarkCase.title: Export shows success before data is ready

benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A success toast appears immediately after queueing the job.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Users waste time looking for a file that does not exist.

expectedFindings.title: Queued export is presented as ready
expectedFindings.description: The toast promises a download before the queued job produces it.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Asynchronous processing is allowed when the UI describes it correctly.

findings.title: Queued exports labeled as ready before downloadable file exists
findings.description: The new export button implementation sends a POST to /api/export and immediately shows a success toast stating "Your export is ready to download" without verifying that a downloadable file actually exists. This violates REQ-UX-3 which requires queued exports be labeled as processing until a downloadable file exists.

benchmarkCase.title: Payment retry loses idempotency key
benchmarkCase.description: A retry generates a new charge identity.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-RETRY-1: Retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The retry creates a random key for every charge.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: One invoice can be charged more than once.

expectedFindings.title: Payment retry generates a new idempotency key
expectedFindings.description: A fresh key permits a duplicate charge for the invoice.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The retry cannot charge a non-existent invoice.

findings.title: Retry uses new idempotency key instead of original
findings.description: REQ-RETRY-1 requires that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key. The patch sets idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID(), generating a new key for each retry instead of reusing the original idempotency key associated with the failed payment. This violates REQ-RETRY-1 and can prevent correct deduplication of retries.

findings.description: The new code unconditionally sets subscription.status = "active" for any existing subscription whose status is not already "active" and then saves it. This will change a subscription with status "cancelled" back to "active" (for example on retry), violating REQ-STATE-2 which requires a cancelled trial remain cancelled and may not be reactivated.

reviewers.title: Invite creation allowed for any team member, not restricted to team administrators
reviewers.description: The new route handler allows any user who has a membership record for the team to create an invitation. It only checks for existence of membership via findMembership(teamId, user.id) and returns 403 if none. There is no check that the membership indicates the user is a team administrator, so non-admin members can create invites, violating REQ-AUTH-1.

reviewers.title: Invitation creation allowed for non-administrators
reviewers.description: The new route handler allows any team member (anyone with a membership) to create invitations. It checks only that findMembership(teamId, user.id) exists; it does not verify that the membership has administrator privileges. This violates REQ-AUTH-1, which requires that only team administrators may create invitations.

reviewers.title: Queued exports labeled as 'ready' before downloadable file exists
reviewers.description: The new export-button.tsx code posts to /api/export and immediately shows toast.success("Your export is ready to download") without verifying that a downloadable file exists. This violates REQ-UX-3, which requires queued exports to be labeled as processing until a downloadable file exists.

reviewers.title: Queued exports labeled as ready-to-download despite no downloadable file
reviewers.description: REQ-UX-3 requires that queued exports be labeled as "processing" until a downloadable file exists. The added exportData function immediately shows a success toast "Your export is ready to download" after posting to /api/export, with no check that a downloadable file exists (no polling, status check, or download URL returned). This causes the UI to indicate the export is ready when it may still be queued/processing, violating REQ-UX-3.

reviewers.title: Retrying a failed payment generates a new idempotency key instead of reusing original
reviewers.description: REQ-RETRY-1 requires that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key. The patch calls crypto.randomUUID() to set idempotencyKey for the charge() call, which creates a new key for each retry rather than reusing the original idempotency key associated with the failed payment attempt.

reviewers.title: Retrying failed payment generates a new idempotency key instead of reusing original
reviewers.description: REQ-RETRY-1 requires that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key. The patch always sets idempotencyKey to crypto.randomUUID() when charging (line: idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID()), which creates a new key for each retry instead of reusing the original idempotency key associated with the failed payment.

reviewers.title: Retry creates a new idempotency key instead of reusing original
reviewers.description: Requirement REQ-RETRY-1 mandates that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key. The patch unconditionally sets idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID(), which generates a new key for each attempt rather than reusing the original idempotency key associated with the failed payment or invoice. This is an explicit violation of REQ-RETRY-1 and can cause duplicate charges or broken retry semantics.

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event recording on manual invoice void
reviewers.description: The route handler for voiding an invoice calls voidInvoice(...) but does not record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id as required by REQ-AUDIT-1. There is no code creating or persisting an audit entry after the void action; only a 404 check and response are present.

reviewers.title: Missing audit event recording when voiding invoice
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 mandates that every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id. The new route handler simply calls voidInvoice and returns the invoice without creating or recording any audit event. There is no code to generate an immutable audit record, include the actor and invoice id, or persist such an event.

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event when voiding invoice
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id. The patch implements voiding logic but contains no code that records any audit event (no call to an audit logger, event store, or database insert for an audit record). There is also no indication that the voidInvoice function itself emits such an immutable audit event. As written, the actor and invoice id are not recorded immutably anywhere in this route.

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event recording on manual invoice void
reviewers.description: The new route handler calls voidInvoice(params.invoiceId, actor.id) and returns the invoice (or 404) but contains no explicit code that records an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id as required by REQ-AUDIT-1. The patch does not show any call to an audit logger, event store, or database insert for an audit record in this route. Unless voidInvoice internally creates an immutable audit event (not visible in this patch), the requirement is not satisfied.

reviewers.title: Cancelled notifications retried
reviewers.description: Code increments attempts and retries sending without checking for 'cancelled' status. REQ-NOTIFY-3 requires cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.

reviewers.title: Cancelled notification may be retried and delivered
reviewers.description: The code increments attempts and calls send() for any notification that is not status === "sent". It does not check for notification.status === "cancelled" (or similar), so cancelled notifications would be retried and potentially delivered. This violates REQ-NOTIFY-3, which requires that cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.

reviewers.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried/delivered

reviewers.title: Sends billing reminders without checking opt-out preference
reviewers.description: The new reminders.ts code fetches the user, builds a reminder, and sends email unconditionally. It contains no check of the user's notification preferences or opt-out status for non-essential billing reminders, so users who have opted out may still be sent reminders, violating REQ-NOTIFY-4.

reviewers.title: Sends billing reminder email without checking user opt-out preference
reviewers.description: The new reminders.ts code fetches a user and unconditionally builds and sends a reminder email: it does not check whether the user has opted out of non-essential billing reminders. According to REQ-NOTIFY-4, users who opted out must not receive such reminders. This behavior directly violates that requirement.

reviewers.title: Display name whitespace validation missing
reviewers.description: Code checks only the string type and overall length, but does not ensure the display name contains 2–80 non-whitespace characters as required. A display name consisting primarily or entirely of whitespace (e.g., "  ") or with leading/trailing whitespace that reduces meaningful characters could pass the length check but violate REQ-VALID-1.

reviewers.title: Whitespace-only displayName accepted
reviewers.description: REQ-VALID-1 requires a display name to contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters. The implementation only checks displayName type and total length (string length between 2 and 80) and does not verify that the name contains non-whitespace characters (e.g., "  ", "\t\n" would pass length checks). Thus whitespace-only values would be accepted, violating the requirement.

reviewers.title: Display name validation does not enforce non-whitespace characters requirement

Inputs such as "  " (two spaces) or strings containing mostly whitespace will pass the current checks even though they violate the requirement.

reviewers.title: Cancelled subscription improperly reactivated by retry
reviewers.description: Code unconditionally sets subscription.status = "active" for any existing subscription unless already "active", then saves it. This allows subscriptions with a prior "cancelled" status to be reactivated, violating the product requirement that a cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry (REQ-STATE-2). The code lacks any check preventing reactivation of subscriptions with status "cancelled" (or similar terminal states) and performs an unconditional state transition to "active".

benchmarkCase.description: Membership is checked but the administrator role is omitted.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUTH-1: Only team administrators may create invitations.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The POST route permits any team member to create an invitation.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation creation does not require an administrator
expectedFindings.description: A regular member can create an invitation because membership is checked without validating the admin role.

distractors.description: The route uses a generic unauthorized error.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: A non-enumerating error message is intentional.

findings.title: Invite creation allowed for any team member, not restricted to team administrators
findings.description: The route handler only verifies that the requester is a team member via findMembership(teamId, user.id) and returns 403 if no membership exists, but it does not check membership role/administrative privileges before calling createInvite. Therefore any team member (not just administrators) can create invitations, violating REQ-AUTH-1 which mandates only team administrators may create invitations.

benchmarkCase.title: Export shows success before data is ready
benchmarkCase.description: The UI reports a queued export as downloadable.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-UX-3: The dashboard must label queued exports as processing until a downloadable file exists.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A success toast appears immediately after queueing the job.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Users waste time looking for a file that does not exist.

expectedFindings.title: Queued export is presented as ready
expectedFindings.description: The toast promises a download before the queued job produces it.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Asynchronous processing is allowed when the UI describes it correctly.

findings.title: Queued exports labeled as 'ready' before downloadable file exists
findings.description: export-button.tsx sends a POST to /api/export and immediately calls toast.success("Your export is ready to download") without confirming a downloadable file exists. This violates REQ-UX-3, which requires queued exports be labeled as processing until a downloadable file exists; the code can mislead users by showing the export as ready while it may still be queued or generating.

benchmarkCase.title: Payment retry loses idempotency key
benchmarkCase.description: A retry generates a new charge identity.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-RETRY-1: Retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The retry creates a random key for every charge.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: One invoice can be charged more than once.

expectedFindings.title: Payment retry generates a new idempotency key
expectedFindings.description: A fresh key permits a duplicate charge for the invoice.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The retry cannot charge a non-existent invoice.

findings.title: Retrying a failed payment generates a new idempotency key instead of reusing original
findings.description: The code calls charge(...) with idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID(), creating a new idempotency key for the retry. REQ-RETRY-1 requires reusing the original idempotency key when retrying a failed payment. Generating a new key breaks the requirement and can cause duplicate charges or incorrect retry semantics.

benchmarkCase.title: Manual invoice void omits audit event
benchmarkCase.description: A required product audit trail is not recorded.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUDIT-1: Every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint voids the invoice but does not write the audit event.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Support and finance cannot determine who voided an invoice.

expectedFindings.title: Manual invoice void has no audit event
expectedFindings.description: The mutation completes without recording the required actor and invoice audit trail.

distractors.description: The response returns the voided invoice.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Returning the updated resource is normal API behavior.

findings.title: Missing immutable audit event recording on manual invoice void
findings.description: The added route handler calls voidInvoice(params.invoiceId, actor.id) and returns the invoice (or 404) but contains no explicit recording of an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id as required by REQ-AUDIT-1. The patch shows no audit logger, event store write, or database insert for an audit record in this route; unless voidInvoice(undefined in this diff) guarantees creation of the required immutable audit event, the requirement is not met.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled notifications are retried
benchmarkCase.description: The retry worker treats cancelled notifications as eligible.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-3: Cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The guard excludes sent notifications but not cancelled ones.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Cancelled messages can reach recipients after cancellation.

expectedFindings.title: Cancelled notifications are eligible for retry
expectedFindings.description: The guard allows cancelled messages to be delivered.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Tracking pending attempts is expected.

findings.title: Cancelled notifications retried
findings.description: The patch increments notification.attempts and calls send(notification) for any notification whose status is not "sent", but does not check for a "cancelled" status. Per REQ-NOTIFY-3, cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried. As written, a notification with status "cancelled" would have attempts incremented and be passed to send(), violating the requirement.

It does not check the membership's role or administrator privileges before calling createInvite, so any team member (not just administrators) could create invitations. This violates REQ-AUTH-1, which requires only team administrators may create invitations.

principal.title: Invitation creation allowed for any team member (admins-only requirement violated)
principal.description: The route handler checks only that the requester is a team member via findMembership(teamId, user.id) and returns 403 if no membership exists, but it does not verify that the membership has administrator privileges before calling createInvite. As written, any team member can create invitations, violating REQ-AUTH-1 which requires that only team administrators may create invitations.

reviewers.title: Queued exports labeled as processing despite immediate 'ready' toast
reviewers.description: REQ-UX-3 requires the dashboard to label queued exports as "processing" until a downloadable file exists. The patch's exportData() sends a POST to /api/export and immediately shows toast.success("Your export is ready to download") without checking export status or whether a downloadable file exists. This directly violates the requirement by signaling readiness prematurely instead of keeping the export labeled as processing while queued.

reviewers.title: Queued exports labeled as ready before downloadable file exists
reviewers.description: The new exportData implementation immediately shows a success toast "Your export is ready to download" after initiating the export request, without verifying that a downloadable export file exists. This violates REQ-UX-3, which requires queued exports be labeled as processing until a downloadable file exists.

reviewers.title: Retrying failed payment generates a new idempotency key instead of reusing original
reviewers.description: The code creates a fresh idempotency key using crypto.randomUUID() when charging: idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID(). Requirement REQ-RETRY-1 mandates that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key. Generating a new UUID on retry violates this requirement and can lead to duplicate charges or inconsistent retry behavior.

reviewers.title: Retry uses a newly generated idempotency key instead of reusing original
reviewers.description: The requirement REQ-RETRY-1 states: "Retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key." The patch always generates a new idempotency key via crypto.randomUUID() when calling charge(), which means retries will not reuse the original idempotency key. This is an explicit violation of the requirement and can cause duplicate charges or failure to recognize the original attempt.

reviewers.title: Retry uses a new idempotency key instead of reusing original

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event recording on manual invoice void
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id. The new route handler calls voidInvoice(...) and returns the invoice but contains no code to create or persist an immutable audit event (no audit log call, no event emission, no append to audit store). There is no evidence the actor and invoice id are recorded immutably as required.

reviewers.title: Manual invoice void does not record immutable audit event
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id. The added route handler calls currentUser and voidInvoice and returns the invoice, but there is no code that creates or records an immutable audit event (no audit API call, no append to audit log, no event creation). Therefore void operations performed through this route will not produce the required audit record.

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event when voiding invoice
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id. There is no code that writes an immutable audit entry (e.g., to an audit log, events table, or append-only store) containing the actor and invoice id.

reviewers.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried
reviewers.description: Code increments attempts and calls send() for any existing notification except for status === "sent". It does not check for status === "cancelled" (or similar), so cancelled notifications will be retried/delivered in violation of REQ-NOTIFY-3, which mandates cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.

reviewers.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried or delivered
reviewers.description: Code increments attempts and calls send() for any notification not in status 'sent', with no check preventing sending when notification.status === 'cancelled'. This allows cancelled notifications to be retried or delivered, violating REQ-NOTIFY-3 which mandates cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried.

Per REQ-NOTIFY-3, cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; this code can retry or deliver cancelled notifications.

reviewers.title: Sends billing reminders without checking user opt-out preference
reviewers.description: The new reminders.ts sends an email to the user unconditionally: it fetches the user, builds a reminder, and calls sendEmail(user.email, message) without checking whether the user has opted out of non-essential billing reminders. This directly violates REQ-NOTIFY-4, which requires that users who have opted out must not receive such reminders.

reviewers.title: Display name length validated but whitespace-only names allowed
reviewers.description: Code checks that displayName is a string and enforces length between 2 and 80 characters, but it does not enforce REQ-VALID-1 requirement that a display name contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters. A string consisting solely of whitespace characters (e.g., "  ") would pass the current length check even though it has fewer than 2 non-whitespace characters.

reviewers.title: Validation counts whitespace characters toward length
reviewers.description: The code enforces displayName length by using displayName.length (counts all characters including whitespace). Requirement REQ-VALID-1 mandates 2–80 non-whitespace characters. The current check allows names with fewer than 2 non-whitespace characters (e.g., "  ", " a"), and can reject or accept incorrectly when leading/trailing/multiple internal whitespace affect length but not non-whitespace count.

reviewers.title: Role update allows demoting the final administrator
reviewers.description: The new code updates a member's role unconditionally and saves it. It does not check whether the member being demoted is the last remaining administrator for the team. This permits a role change that would leave the team with zero administrators, violating REQ-REGRESS-1 which mandates rejecting updates that would demote the final admin.

reviewers.title: Allows demoting the last administrator
reviewers.description: The patch updates a team member's role without checking whether this is the final administrator. Per REQ-REGRESS-1, role updates that would demote the final admin must be rejected. The new code simply assigns member.role = role and saves, so it can remove the last admin and leave the team with no administrators.

reviewers.title: Final administrator demotion not prevented
reviewers.description: The patch updates a member's role and saves it without checking whether this change would remove the last remaining administrator from the team. REQ-REGRESS-1 requires rejecting role updates that would demote the final admin. The new code does not verify the count or existence of other administrators and thus can demote the final admin, violating the requirement.

reviewers.title: Starter team invitation allows creating invitations without enforcing 3-member limit
reviewers.description: Function inviteToTeam creates and sends an invitation for any team without checking the current active member count or team plan. Requirement REQ-PLAN-2 mandates that starter teams may have at most three active members and that invitations which would exceed this limit must be rejected. The implementation: - Retrieves team via getTeam(teamId) but does not inspect team.plan or team.type to determine if it is a starter team. - Does not check team.activeMemberCount (or equivalent) to determine whether adding a new member would exceed the 3-member limit. - Always calls createInvitation and sendEmail, thereby allowing over-limit invitations to be created and sent. This is an explicit violation of REQ-PLAN-2.

reviewers.title: Invitations do not enforce starter team member limit
reviewers.description: Requirement REQ-PLAN-2 states that starter teams may have at most three active members and that invitations exceeding that limit must be rejected. The new inviteToTeam function fetches the team and validates the email but does not check the current number of active members nor whether the team is a starter plan. As a result, it will create and send invitations even when the team already has three or more active members, violating the requirement.

reviewers.title: Cancelled trial may be reactivated by retry
reviewers.description: Code unconditionally sets subscription.status = "active" except when already "active", and saves the subscription. There is no check preventing reactivation of subscriptions in cancelled state. This violates REQ-STATE-2 which requires a cancelled trial remain cancelled and not be reactivated by retry.

reviewers.title: Cancelled trial can be reactivated by retry
reviewers.description: The patch loads a subscription and unconditionally sets status to "active" when it is not already "active". There is no check preventing reactivation of subscriptions that were previously cancelled or marked as trial-cancelled. This directly violates REQ-STATE-2, which requires that a cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry.

reviewers.title: Cancelled trial can be reactivated by retry

reviewers.title: Cancelled trial may be reactivated by retry

benchmarkCase.title: Member can create team invitations
benchmarkCase.description: Membership is checked but the administrator role is omitted.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUTH-1: Only team administrators may create invitations.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The POST route permits any team member to create an invitation.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Regular members can expand a team without authorization.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation creation does not require an administrator
expectedFindings.description: A regular member can create an invitation because membership is checked without validating the admin role.

distractors.description: The route uses a generic unauthorized error.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: A non-enumerating error message is intentional.

findings.title: Invitation creation allowed for any team member (admins-only requirement violated)
findings.description: The route handler checks only that the requester is a team member via findMembership(teamId, user.id) and returns 403 if no membership exists, but it does not verify that the membership has administrator privileges before calling createInvite. As written, any team member can create invitations, violating REQ-AUTH-1 which requires that only team administrators may create invitations.

benchmarkCase.title: Export shows success before data is ready
benchmarkCase.description: The UI reports a queued export as downloadable.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-UX-3: The dashboard must label queued exports as processing until a downloadable file exists.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A success toast appears immediately after queueing the job.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Users waste time looking for a file that does not exist.

expectedFindings.title: Queued export is presented as ready
expectedFindings.description: The toast promises a download before the queued job produces it.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Asynchronous processing is allowed when the UI describes it correctly.

findings.title: Queued exports labeled as processing despite immediate 'ready' toast
findings.description: REQ-UX-3 requires the dashboard to label queued exports as "processing" until a downloadable file exists. The patch's exportData() sends a POST to /api/export and immediately shows toast.success("Your export is ready to download") without checking export status or whether a downloadable file exists. This signals readiness prematurely instead of keeping the export labeled as processing while queued, violating the requirement.

benchmarkCase.title: Payment retry loses idempotency key
benchmarkCase.description: A retry generates a new charge identity.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-RETRY-1: Retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The retry creates a random key for every charge.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: One invoice can be charged more than once.

expectedFindings.title: Payment retry generates a new idempotency key
expectedFindings.description: A fresh key permits a duplicate charge for the invoice.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The retry cannot charge a non-existent invoice.

findings.title: Retrying failed payment generates a new idempotency key instead of reusing original
findings.description: The patched code calls charge(...) with idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID(), which always generates a new idempotency key. Requirement REQ-RETRY-1 mandates that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key. Generating a new UUID on retry violates this requirement and can cause duplicate charges or prevent the system from recognizing and de-duplicating the retried attempt.

benchmarkCase.title: Manual invoice void omits audit event
benchmarkCase.description: A required product audit trail is not recorded.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUDIT-1: Every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint voids the invoice but does not write the audit event.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Support and finance cannot determine who voided an invoice.

expectedFindings.title: Manual invoice void has no audit event
expectedFindings.description: The mutation completes without recording the required actor and invoice audit trail.

distractors.description: The response returns the voided invoice.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Returning the updated resource is normal API behavior.

findings.title: Missing immutable audit event recording on manual invoice void
findings.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id. The new route handler calls currentUser(request) and voidInvoice(params.invoiceId, actor.id) but contains no code to create or persist an immutable audit event (no audit log call, event emission, or append to an audit store). There is no evidence the actor and invoice id are recorded immutably as required.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled notifications are retried
benchmarkCase.description: The retry worker treats cancelled notifications as eligible.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-3: Cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The guard excludes sent notifications but not cancelled ones.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Cancelled messages can reach recipients after cancellation.

expectedFindings.title: Cancelled notifications are eligible for retry
expectedFindings.description: The guard allows cancelled messages to be delivered.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Tracking pending attempts is expected.

findings.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried or delivered
findings.description: The patch increments attempts and calls send() for any fetched notification unless its status is "sent". There is no check preventing operation when notification.status === "cancelled" (or an equivalent cancelled state), so cancelled notifications can be retried or delivered. This violates REQ-NOTIFY-3, which requires that cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.

expectedFindings.title: Billing reminder ignores opt-out preference
expectedFindings.description: The sender delivers a non-essential reminder without a preference check.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The sender must not send to a missing user.

findings.title: Sends billing reminders without checking user opt-out preference
findings.description: The new reminders.ts fetches the user, builds a reminder, and calls sendEmail(user.email, message) unconditionally. There is no check of the user's notification preferences or opt-out status for non-essential billing reminders. This violates REQ-NOTIFY-4, which requires that users who have opted out of non-essential billing reminders must not receive them.

principal.title: Retry of failed payment generates a new idempotency key instead of reusing original

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event recording on manual invoice void

reviewers.title: Retries performed without checking for 'cancelled' status
reviewers.description: Code increments attempts and calls send() for a notification regardless of whether its status is 'cancelled'. REQ-NOTIFY-3 mandates that cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried. The patch only checks for status === 'sent' and allows any other status (including 'cancelled') to be retried.

reviewers.title: Cancelled notification may be retried/delivered

The code also lacks an explicit guard preventing retries for non-pending statuses.

reviewers.title: Display name length validated but does not enforce non-whitespace characters
reviewers.description: The new route checks displayName is a string and enforces length between 2 and 80 characters, but it validates length using displayName.length which counts all characters including whitespace. REQ-VALID-1 requires 2–80 non-whitespace characters. The implementation does not trim or remove whitespace nor verify there are at least 2 non-whitespace characters, so inputs like "  a" or "   " (multiple spaces) could pass length checks incorrectly.

reviewers.title: Whitespace-only display names accepted

The new validation only checks the string length (displayName.length) and type, so a string of 2–80 whitespace characters (e.g., "  ") would pass but contains 0 non-whitespace characters, violating the requirement.

reviewers.description: The patch updates a member's role directly and saves it without checking whether this change would remove the last remaining administrator on the team. This allows demotion of the final admin and therefore violates REQ-REGRESS-1.

reviewers.title: No check against starter team member limit before creating invitation

reviewers.title: Cancelled trial can be reactivated by retry

This includes subscriptions previously marked as "cancelled" (trial cancelled). That allows a cancelled trial to be reactivated by retry, violating REQ-STATE-2 which requires a cancelled trial remain cancelled and may not be reactivated.

This violates REQ-STATE-2: "A cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry."

REQ-UX-3 requires queued exports be labeled as "processing" until a downloadable file exists; this code prematurely marks exports as ready.

distractors.description: The response returns the voided invoice.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Returning the updated resource is normal API behavior.

findings.title: Missing immutable audit event recording on manual invoice void
findings.description: The new route handler for manual invoice void (apps/reference-saas/app/api/invoices/[invoiceId]/void/route.ts) invokes voidInvoice(params.invoiceId, actor.id) and returns the invoice, but does not record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id as required by REQ-AUDIT-1. There is no call to an audit/logging service, no creation of an immutable event record, and no persistent audit data written in this patch.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled notifications are retried
benchmarkCase.description: The retry worker treats cancelled notifications as eligible.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-3: Cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The guard excludes sent notifications but not cancelled ones.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Cancelled messages can reach recipients after cancellation.

expectedFindings.title: Cancelled notifications are eligible for retry
expectedFindings.description: The guard allows cancelled messages to be delivered.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Tracking pending attempts is expected.

findings.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried or delivered
findings.description: The patch increments notification.attempts and calls send(notification) for any notification that exists unless its status is "sent". It does not check for a "cancelled" status (or restrict to "pending"), so notifications marked cancelled could be retried or delivered, violating REQ-NOTIFY-3 which requires cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.

benchmarkCase.title: Opted-out users receive billing notices
benchmarkCase.description: The sender omits notification preferences.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-4: Users opted out of non-essential billing reminders must not receive them.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A billing reminder is sent without reading the opt-out preference.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: The product disregards a user's communication choice.

expectedFindings.title: Billing reminder ignores opt-out preference
expectedFindings.description: The sender delivers a non-essential reminder without a preference check.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The sender must not send to a missing user.

findings.title: Sends billing reminders without checking opt-out preference
findings.description: apps/reference-saas/lib/reminders.ts constructs and sends reminder emails unconditionally: it fetches the user, builds a reminder, and calls sendEmail(user.email, message) with no check of the user's preference for non-essential billing reminders. This violates REQ-NOTIFY-4, which requires that users who opted out of non-essential billing reminders must not receive them.

benchmarkCase.title: Blank display names are accepted
benchmarkCase.description: Whitespace-only profile names pass length validation.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-VALID-1: A display name must contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint checks raw string length instead of trimmed content.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Profiles can have unusable blank identities.

expectedFindings.title: Display name lacks trimmed validation
expectedFindings.description: Whitespace-only names pass the length check.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Rejecting invalid types satisfies the API contract.

findings.title: Validation does not enforce non-whitespace characters in displayName
findings.description: The new route verifies displayName is a string and that displayName.length is between 2 and 80, but it does not ensure those characters are non-whitespace. As a result, strings consisting solely (or largely) of whitespace characters (for example "  " or "    a") can satisfy the length check while containing fewer than 2 non-whitespace characters, violating REQ-VALID-1.

benchmarkCase.title: Role update regresses last-admin safeguard
benchmarkCase.description: The new role update path can demote the final administrator.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-REGRESS-1: A team must retain at least one administrator; role updates that would demote the final admin must be rejected.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The role update writes the requested role without checking remaining administrators.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: A team can become permanently unmanaged.

expectedFindings.title: Role change can demote the final administrator
expectedFindings.description: The update lacks the required last-admin safety check.

distractors.description: The target membership is checked for existence.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Rejecting an unknown membership is required input handling.

findings.title: Allows demotion of final administrator
findings.description: The patch unconditionally sets member.role = role and persists it without checking whether that update would remove the last remaining administrator for the team. REQ-REGRESS-1 requires rejecting role updates that would demote the final admin; this code permits demoting the final admin and can leave a team with zero administrators.

benchmarkCase.title: Starter plan seat limit is bypassed
benchmarkCase.description: The invitation flow omits the plan seat check.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-PLAN-2: Starter teams may have at most three active members; over-limit invitations must be rejected.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: An invitation is created without checking active seats against the Starter limit.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Customers can receive paid capacity without upgrading.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation ignores Starter seat limit
expectedFindings.description: The flow sends an invitation without checking the team's active seat count.

distractors.description: The email is checked for an at sign.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Basic email validation is independent of capacity enforcement.

findings.title: Missing enforcement of starter-team member limit before creating invitation
findings.description: REQ-PLAN-2 requires that starter teams may have at most three active members and that invitations which would exceed that limit must be rejected. The patched inviteToTeam function fetches the team but does not check the team's plan/type or current active member count before creating and sending an invitation. As a result, invitations that would cause a starter team to exceed three active members can be created and sent, violating REQ-PLAN-2.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled trial can be reactivated
benchmarkCase.description: The retry handler treats cancelled subscriptions as recoverable.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-STATE-2: A cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: Every non-active subscription is set to active.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: A user can be restored to a service they explicitly cancelled.

expectedFindings.title: Retry reactivates cancelled trials
expectedFindings.description: The handler changes cancelled trials to active.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Avoiding a redundant write is correct.

findings.title: Cancelled trial reactivated by billing patch
findings.description: The new billing code unconditionally sets subscription.status = "active" for any existing subscription that is not already active, without checking for a prior "cancelled" state. This would transition subscriptions marked as cancelled back to active, allowing a cancelled trial to be reactivated by retry and violating REQ-STATE-2: "A cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry."

reviewers.title: Dashboard labels queued exports as ready before downloadable file exists
reviewers.description: REQ-UX-3 requires that the dashboard label queued exports as "processing" until a downloadable file exists. The patch's exportData function posts to /api/export and immediately shows a success toast "Your export is ready to download" without checking whether a downloadable file exists or whether the export is still queued/processing. This directly violates REQ-UX-3 by marking exports as ready prematurely.

reviewers.title: Retrying failed payment does not reuse original idempotency key
reviewers.description: The new implementation generates a fresh idempotency key via crypto.randomUUID() when charging an invoice. Requirement REQ-RETRY-1 mandates that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key. Using a new random key on retry violates this requirement and may lead to duplicate charges.

reviewers.title: Retrying a failed payment generates a new idempotency key instead of reusing original
reviewers.description: The new payments implementation always sets idempotencyKey to crypto.randomUUID() when calling charge(...). Requirement REQ-RETRY-1 mandates that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key. The patch therefore violates this requirement because it does not retrieve or pass the original idempotency key for retries.

reviewers.title: Invitations not blocked when starter team already has three active members
reviewers.description: REQ-PLAN-2 requires that starter teams may have at most three active members and that over-limit invitations must be rejected. The new inviteToTeam function does not check the team's plan/type or the current count of active members before creating an invitation. It always creates an invitation for the given teamId and email, thereby allowing invitations to be created even when a starter team already has three active members. This is an explicit violation of the requirement.

reviewers.title: Invitations do not enforce starter-team member limit
reviewers.description: Requirement REQ-PLAN-2 states: "Starter teams may have at most three active members; over-limit invitations must be rejected." The new inviteToTeam function does not check the current number of active members on the team before creating an invitation. It fetches the team and validates email, but it immediately creates an invitation regardless of team size, allowing invitations that would exceed the three-member limit. This is an explicit violation of the requirement: over-limit invitations are not rejected.

benchmarkCase.description: Membership is checked but the administrator role is omitted.

benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The POST route permits any team member to create an invitation.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Regular members can expand a team without authorization.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation creation does not require an administrator
expectedFindings.description: A regular member can create an invitation because membership is checked without validating the admin role.

distractors.description: The route uses a generic unauthorized error.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: A non-enumerating error message is intentional.

findings.title: Invitation creation allowed for non-administrators
findings.description: The new route at apps/reference-saas/app/api/teams/[teamId]/invites/route.ts only checks that the requester has a team membership (findMembership) and returns 403 for non-members, but does not verify that the membership has administrator privileges before calling createInvite. This allows any team member to create invitations, violating REQ-AUTH-1 which requires that only team administrators may create invitations.

benchmarkCase.title: Export shows success before data is ready
benchmarkCase.description: The UI reports a queued export as downloadable.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-UX-3: The dashboard must label queued exports as processing until a downloadable file exists.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A success toast appears immediately after queueing the job.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Users waste time looking for a file that does not exist.

expectedFindings.title: Queued export is presented as ready
expectedFindings.description: The toast promises a download before the queued job produces it.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Asynchronous processing is allowed when the UI describes it correctly.

findings.title: Dashboard marks exports as ready immediately without verifying downloadable file
findings.description: The new exportData implementation sends a POST to /api/export and immediately displays a success toast "Your export is ready to download" without checking whether a downloadable file exists or whether the export remains queued/processing on the server. This behavior violates REQ-UX-3, which requires queued exports be labeled as "processing" until a downloadable file exists.

benchmarkCase.title: Payment retry loses idempotency key
benchmarkCase.description: A retry generates a new charge identity.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-RETRY-1: Retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The retry creates a random key for every charge.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: One invoice can be charged more than once.

expectedFindings.title: Payment retry generates a new idempotency key
expectedFindings.description: A fresh key permits a duplicate charge for the invoice.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The retry cannot charge a non-existent invoice.

findings.title: Retrying failed payment does not reuse original idempotency key
findings.description: The patched function always generates a new idempotency key via crypto.randomUUID() when calling charge({ ... idempotencyKey }). Requirement REQ-RETRY-1 mandates that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key; the patch does not retrieve or pass the original key for retries, violating the requirement and risking duplicate charges.

benchmarkCase.title: Manual invoice void omits audit event
benchmarkCase.description: A required product audit trail is not recorded.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUDIT-1: Every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint voids the invoice but does not write the audit event.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Support and finance cannot determine who voided an invoice.

expectedFindings.title: Manual invoice void has no audit event
expectedFindings.description: The mutation completes without recording the required actor and invoice audit trail.

distractors.description: The response returns the voided invoice.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Returning the updated resource is normal API behavior.

findings.title: Missing immutable audit event when voiding invoice
findings.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id. The new route handler (apps/reference-saas/app/api/invoices/[invoiceId]/void/route.ts) calls voidInvoice(params.invoiceId, actor.id) and returns the invoice, but contains no code to create or persist an immutable audit event (no audit/log API call, no write to an audit store, and no verification that voidInvoice recorded such an event). Therefore the implementation does not demonstrate the required immutable audit recording.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled notifications are retried
benchmarkCase.description: The retry worker treats cancelled notifications as eligible.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-3: Cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The guard excludes sent notifications but not cancelled ones.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Cancelled messages can reach recipients after cancellation.

expectedFindings.title: Cancelled notifications are eligible for retry
expectedFindings.description: The guard allows cancelled messages to be delivered.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Tracking pending attempts is expected.

findings.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried or delivered
findings.description: The patch retrieves a notification and, except when status === "sent", increments attempts and calls send(). There is no check preventing action when notification.status === "cancelled" (or other non-'sent' states). As a result, cancelled notifications can be retried or delivered, violating REQ-NOTIFY-3 which requires that cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried and only pending notifications may be retried.

findings.title: Billing reminders sent without checking opt-out preference

reviewers.title: Queued exports labeled as processing until downloadable file exists not enforced
reviewers.description: REQ-UX-3 requires the dashboard to label queued exports as "processing" until a downloadable file exists. The added exportData function immediately shows a success toast "Your export is ready to download" right after sending the POST /api/export request, without checking whether a downloadable file actually exists or whether the export is still queued/processing. This causes the UI to indicate the export is ready instead of labeling it as processing, violating REQ-UX-3.

The code provides no polling, status check, or download link validation before indicating readiness.

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event on manual invoice void
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id. There is no evidence the actor and invoice id are recorded immutably as required.

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event recording on manual invoice void

reviewers.title: Retries performed regardless of 'cancelled' status
reviewers.description: The new code increments attempts and calls send() for any notification that exists and is not 'sent'. It only guards against notifications with status === 'sent', but does not check for status === 'cancelled'. As a result, cancelled notifications would have their attempts incremented and be retried/delivered, violating REQ-NOTIFY-3 which mandates cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried.

reviewers.title: Cancelled notifications are retried/delivered
reviewers.description: The patch increments attempts and calls send(notification) for any notification that exists and is not already 'sent'. It does not check for a 'cancelled' status. Thus cancelled notifications could be delivered or retried, violating REQ-NOTIFY-3 which mandates that cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.

reviewers.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried

It does not check for status === "cancelled" (or similar) and thus will retry notifications that have been cancelled, violating REQ-NOTIFY-3 which forbids delivering or retrying cancelled notifications. The code only short-circuits "sent" status, allowing cancelled notifications to be retried.

reviewers.title: Allows demoting the final administrator
reviewers.description: The patch unconditionally updates a member's role and saves it. There is no check to ensure the team will still have at least one administrator after the change. This violates REQ-REGRESS-1 which requires rejecting role updates that would demote the final admin.

reviewers.title: Role update may remove final administrator

REQ-REGRESS-1 requires that role updates that would demote the final admin must be rejected. The patch fetches the membership, sets member.role = role, and saves it with no check for other admins or for whether this member is the last admin, so it can remove the sole admin.
