This allows a previously cancelled trial subscription to be changed back to active, violating REQ-STATE-2 which requires that a cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry.

principal.title: Cancelled trial can be reactivated by retry
principal.description: The new billing code unconditionally sets subscription.status = "active" for any existing subscription that is not already "active", without checking for a prior "cancelled" state. This allows subscriptions previously marked as cancelled to be reactivated by retry, violating REQ-STATE-2 which requires that a cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated.

benchmarkCase.title: Member can create team invitations
benchmarkCase.description: Membership is checked but the administrator role is omitted.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUTH-1: Only team administrators may create invitations.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The POST route permits any team member to create an invitation.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Regular members can expand a team without authorization.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation creation does not require an administrator
expectedFindings.description: A regular member can create an invitation because membership is checked without validating the admin role.

distractors.description: The route uses a generic unauthorized error.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: A non-enumerating error message is intentional.

findings.title: Invitation creation allowed for non-administrators
findings.description: The new invites route only checks for the existence of a membership via findMembership(teamId, user.id) and returns 403 if none exists. It does not verify the membership's role or administrator status before calling createInvite. As a result, any team member (including non-admins) can create invitations, violating REQ-AUTH-1 which requires that only team administrators may create invitations.

benchmarkCase.title: Export shows success before data is ready
benchmarkCase.description: The UI reports a queued export as downloadable.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-UX-3: The dashboard must label queued exports as processing until a downloadable file exists.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A success toast appears immediately after queueing the job.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Users waste time looking for a file that does not exist.

expectedFindings.title: Queued export is presented as ready
expectedFindings.description: The toast promises a download before the queued job produces it.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Asynchronous processing is allowed when the UI describes it correctly.

findings.title: Dashboard indicates export is ready without verifying downloadable file exists
findings.description: The new exportData function sends POST /api/export and immediately displays a success toast "Your export is ready to download" without checking export status or confirming a downloadable file is available. REQ-UX-3 requires queued exports be labeled as "processing" until a downloadable file exists; this code can prematurely mark exports as ready.

benchmarkCase.title: Payment retry loses idempotency key
benchmarkCase.description: A retry generates a new charge identity.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-RETRY-1: Retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The retry creates a random key for every charge.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: One invoice can be charged more than once.

expectedFindings.title: Payment retry generates a new idempotency key
expectedFindings.description: A fresh key permits a duplicate charge for the invoice.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The retry cannot charge a non-existent invoice.

findings.title: Retry creates a new idempotency key instead of reusing original
findings.description: REQ-RETRY-1 requires that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key. The patch calls crypto.randomUUID() and passes that value as idempotencyKey to charge(), so each retry will generate and use a new idempotency key instead of reusing the original one associated with the failed attempt. This violates REQ-RETRY-1 and can break idempotency guarantees.

benchmarkCase.title: Manual invoice void omits audit event
benchmarkCase.description: A required product audit trail is not recorded.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUDIT-1: Every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint voids the invoice but does not write the audit event.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Support and finance cannot determine who voided an invoice.

expectedFindings.title: Manual invoice void has no audit event
expectedFindings.description: The mutation completes without recording the required actor and invoice audit trail.

distractors.description: The response returns the voided invoice.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Returning the updated resource is normal API behavior.

findings.title: Missing immutable audit event on manual invoice void
findings.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id. The added handler at apps/reference-saas/app/api/invoices/[invoiceId]/void/route.ts calls currentUser(request) and voidInvoice(params.invoiceId, actor.id) and returns the invoice, but contains no code that creates or persists an immutable audit record (no call to an audit logger/service, no append to an audit table/stream, and no explicit persistence of actor and invoice id as an immutable event). Unless voidInvoice guarantees creation of such an immutable audit event (not shown in the patch), the route does not satisfy REQ-AUDIT-1.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled notifications are retried
benchmarkCase.description: The retry worker treats cancelled notifications as eligible.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-3: Cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The guard excludes sent notifications but not cancelled ones.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Cancelled messages can reach recipients after cancellation.

expectedFindings.title: Cancelled notifications are eligible for retry
expectedFindings.description: The guard allows cancelled messages to be delivered.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Tracking pending attempts is expected.

findings.title: Cancelled notifications are retried/delivered
findings.description: The patched code only guards against notifications with status === 'sent' and then increments attempts and calls send(notification) for any other existing notification. It does not check for a 'cancelled' status, so cancelled notifications would have their attempts incremented and be passed to send(), violating REQ-NOTIFY-3 which requires that cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried.

benchmarkCase.title: Opted-out users receive billing notices
benchmarkCase.description: The sender omits notification preferences.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-4: Users opted out of non-essential billing reminders must not receive them.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A billing reminder is sent without reading the opt-out preference.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: The product disregards a user's communication choice.

expectedFindings.title: Billing reminder ignores opt-out preference
expectedFindings.description: The sender delivers a non-essential reminder without a preference check.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The sender must not send to a missing user.

findings.title: Sends billing reminders without checking opt-out preference
findings.description: apps/reference-saas/lib/reminders.ts unconditionally builds and sends an email reminder after fetching the user (lines 1-7). The code never checks the user's opt-out or notification preferences before calling sendEmail(user.email, message), so users who have opted out of non-essential billing reminders may still receive them.

benchmarkCase.title: Blank display names are accepted
benchmarkCase.description: Whitespace-only profile names pass length validation.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-VALID-1: A display name must contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint checks raw string length instead of trimmed content.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Profiles can have unusable blank identities.

expectedFindings.title: Display name lacks trimmed validation
expectedFindings.description: Whitespace-only names pass the length check.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Rejecting invalid types satisfies the API contract.

findings.title: Display name validation allows whitespace-only names
findings.description: The new route checks that displayName is a string and that displayName.length is between 2 and 80, but it does not verify that the characters are non-whitespace. A value consisting solely of whitespace (for example, "  ") has length >= 2 and would pass the checks, violating REQ-VALID-1 which requires 2–80 non-whitespace characters.

benchmarkCase.title: Role update regresses last-admin safeguard
benchmarkCase.description: The new role update path can demote the final administrator.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-REGRESS-1: A team must retain at least one administrator; role updates that would demote the final admin must be rejected.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The role update writes the requested role without checking remaining administrators.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: A team can become permanently unmanaged.

expectedFindings.title: Role change can demote the final administrator
expectedFindings.description: The update lacks the required last-admin safety check.

distractors.description: The target membership is checked for existence.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Rejecting an unknown membership is required input handling.

findings.title: Allows demoting the final administrator
findings.description: The patch unconditionally updates a member's role and persists it without verifying whether the team would retain at least one administrator afterward. There is no check for other administrators or whether the target member is the team's last admin, so the change can demote the sole administrator, violating REQ-REGRESS-1 which requires rejecting role updates that would demote the final admin.

benchmarkCase.title: Starter plan seat limit is bypassed
benchmarkCase.description: The invitation flow omits the plan seat check.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-PLAN-2: Starter teams may have at most three active members; over-limit invitations must be rejected.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: An invitation is created without checking active seats against the Starter limit.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Customers can receive paid capacity without upgrading.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation ignores Starter seat limit
expectedFindings.description: The flow sends an invitation without checking the team's active seat count.

distractors.description: The email is checked for an at sign.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Basic email validation is independent of capacity enforcement.

findings.title: Starter team invitation over-limit not enforced
findings.description: REQ-PLAN-2 requires starter teams may have at most three active members and that invitations that would exceed that limit must be rejected. The new inviteToTeam implementation in apps/reference-saas/lib/invitations.ts does not check the team's plan (starter vs other) nor the team's current active member count before creating/sending an invitation. It unconditionally calls createInvitation and sendEmail, allowing invitations that could put a starter team over the 3-member limit.

reviewers.title: Idempotency key not reused when retrying failed payment
reviewers.description: Code always generates a new idempotency key (crypto.randomUUID()) when creating a charge. The requirement REQ-RETRY-1 mandates that retries of a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key; this patch does not preserve or reuse any prior idempotency key and therefore violates the requirement.

reviewers.title: Retry uses new idempotency key instead of original key
reviewers.description: The code always generates a new idempotency key via crypto.randomUUID() when charging (idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID()). REQ-RETRY-1 requires that retrying a failed payment reuse the original idempotency key. This implementation will violate that requirement and can cause duplicate charges or failure to recognize retries.

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event for manual invoice void
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void records an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id. The added route handler calls voidInvoice and returns the invoice but contains no code to record an audit event (no audit logging, append-only store write, or similar). There is no evidence that voidInvoice records such an immutable audit event, nor does the route emit one including actor and invoice id. Therefore the change violates REQ-AUDIT-1.

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event when voiding invoice
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id. The new route handler voids the invoice but does not create any audit record or emit an immutable audit event. There is no call to an audit logging function, no persistence of an audit event, and no inclusion of actor/invoice id in any audit store. As written, voiding an invoice will not satisfy the requirement to record an immutable audit event.

reviewers.title: Display name validation allows whitespace-only names
reviewers.description: The new route checks displayName length using displayName.length, but REQ-VALID-1 requires a display name contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters. The patch does not trim or otherwise ensure non-whitespace characters; a string of two or more spaces (or other whitespace) will pass the length check but violate the requirement.

reviewers.title: Missing explicit rejection for empty/whitespace-only display name message
reviewers.description: The error messages returned ('Name required' and 'Name must be 2-80 characters') do not communicate the non-whitespace-character requirement mandated by REQ-VALID-1. The code does not enforce or report that display name must contain non-whitespace characters.

reviewers.title: Missing check for non-whitespace characters in display name
reviewers.description: The requirement REQ-VALID-1 mandates that a display name must contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters. A string consisting entirely or mostly of whitespace (for example, "  ") would pass the length check but violate the requirement.

reviewers.title: Role update allows demoting the final administrator
reviewers.description: The patch updates a member's role and saves it without checking whether that member is the team's last administrator. REQ-REGRESS-1 requires rejecting role updates that would demote the final admin; the new code will permit demoting (or removing admin privileges from) the sole remaining admin, violating the requirement.

reviewers.title: Role update allows demoting the last administrator
reviewers.description: The new implementation directly sets member.role = role and saves without checking whether this would remove the team's last administrator. REQ-REGRESS-1 requires rejecting any role update that would demote the final admin; the patch contains no logic to count remaining admins or prevent demotion of the last admin, so it can leave a team with zero administrators.

reviewers.title: No check preventing demotion of final administrator

The new code (getMembership -> set role -> saveMembership) contains no logic to count current admins or to prevent demoting the last admin, so it could remove the final administrator.

reviewers.title: Invitations to starter teams not limited to three active members (REQ-PLAN-2)
reviewers.description: The new inviteToTeam function does not check the current number of active members on the target team before creating an invitation. REQ-PLAN-2 requires that starter teams may have at most three active members and that invitations beyond that limit must be rejected. The patch simply fetches the team and validates the email, then creates and sends an invitation without enforcing the member-count limit, allowing over-limit invitations to be created and sent.

Thus over-limit invitations can be created and sent for starter teams, violating the requirement.

benchmarkCase.title: Member can create team invitations
benchmarkCase.description: Membership is checked but the administrator role is omitted.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUTH-1: Only team administrators may create invitations.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The POST route permits any team member to create an invitation.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Regular members can expand a team without authorization.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation creation does not require an administrator
expectedFindings.description: A regular member can create an invitation because membership is checked without validating the admin role.

distractors.description: The route uses a generic unauthorized error.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: A non-enumerating error message is intentional.

findings.title: Invite creation allows non-admin team members to create invitations
findings.description: The new route only verifies that the user has a membership (findMembership(teamId, user.id)) and returns 403 if none exists. It does not check that the membership grants administrator privileges before calling createInvite, so any team member could create invites. This violates REQ-AUTH-1 which requires that only team administrators may create invitations.

benchmarkCase.title: Export shows success before data is ready
benchmarkCase.description: The UI reports a queued export as downloadable.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-UX-3: The dashboard must label queued exports as processing until a downloadable file exists.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A success toast appears immediately after queueing the job.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Users waste time looking for a file that does not exist.

expectedFindings.title: Queued export is presented as ready
expectedFindings.description: The toast promises a download before the queued job produces it.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Asynchronous processing is allowed when the UI describes it correctly.

findings.title: Queued exports labeled as ready before downloadable file exists
findings.description: REQ-UX-3 requires queued exports to be labeled as "processing" until a downloadable file exists. The new exportData function posts to /api/export and immediately displays a success toast: "Your export is ready to download", without verifying that a downloadable file is available. This can report exports as ready while they are still queued, violating REQ-UX-3.

benchmarkCase.title: Payment retry loses idempotency key
benchmarkCase.description: A retry generates a new charge identity.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-RETRY-1: Retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The retry creates a random key for every charge.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: One invoice can be charged more than once.

expectedFindings.title: Payment retry generates a new idempotency key
expectedFindings.description: A fresh key permits a duplicate charge for the invoice.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The retry cannot charge a non-existent invoice.

findings.title: Idempotency key not reused when retrying failed payment
findings.description: The patch always generates a fresh idempotency key (idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID()) when creating a charge. REQ-RETRY-1 requires that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key; this implementation neither retrieves nor reuses any previous idempotency key and therefore violates the requirement.

benchmarkCase.title: Manual invoice void omits audit event
benchmarkCase.description: A required product audit trail is not recorded.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUDIT-1: Every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint voids the invoice but does not write the audit event.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Support and finance cannot determine who voided an invoice.

expectedFindings.title: Manual invoice void has no audit event
expectedFindings.description: The mutation completes without recording the required actor and invoice audit trail.

distractors.description: The response returns the voided invoice.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Returning the updated resource is normal API behavior.

findings.title: Missing immutable audit event for manual invoice void
findings.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id. The added route handler calls voidInvoice and returns the invoice but contains no code that records such an immutable audit event (no audit log call, no append-only store write, and no explicit persistence of actor+invoice id). The patch also provides no evidence that voidInvoice itself emits the required immutable audit event. Consequently the change appears to violate REQ-AUDIT-1.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled notifications are retried
benchmarkCase.description: The retry worker treats cancelled notifications as eligible.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-3: Cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The guard excludes sent notifications but not cancelled ones.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Cancelled messages can reach recipients after cancellation.

expectedFindings.title: Cancelled notifications are eligible for retry
expectedFindings.description: The guard allows cancelled messages to be delivered.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Tracking pending attempts is expected.

findings.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried or delivered
findings.description: The patch fetches a notification and only skips processing when notification.status === "sent". It then increments notification.attempts and calls send(notification) for any existing notification that is not "sent", without checking for a "cancelled" (or equivalent) status. Therefore cancelled notifications could be retried or delivered, violating REQ-NOTIFY-3 which requires that cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.

benchmarkCase.title: Opted-out users receive billing notices
benchmarkCase.description: The sender omits notification preferences.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-4: Users opted out of non-essential billing reminders must not receive them.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A billing reminder is sent without reading the opt-out preference.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: The product disregards a user's communication choice.

expectedFindings.title: Billing reminder ignores opt-out preference
expectedFindings.description: The sender delivers a non-essential reminder without a preference check.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The sender must not send to a missing user.

findings.title: Sends non-essential billing reminders despite user opt-out
findings.description: The added file apps/reference-saas/lib/reminders.ts unconditionally fetches the user, builds a billing reminder, and calls sendEmail(user.email, message) without checking the user's notification preferences or opt-out status. This can result in non-essential billing reminders being sent to users who have opted out, violating REQ-NOTIFY-4.

benchmarkCase.title: Blank display names are accepted
benchmarkCase.description: Whitespace-only profile names pass length validation.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-VALID-1: A display name must contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint checks raw string length instead of trimmed content.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Profiles can have unusable blank identities.

expectedFindings.title: Display name lacks trimmed validation
expectedFindings.description: Whitespace-only names pass the length check.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Rejecting invalid types satisfies the API contract.

findings.title: Display name validation allows whitespace-only names
findings.description: The handler validates displayName by type and length only. It accepts any string of length 2–80, but REQ-VALID-1 requires 2–80 non-whitespace characters. A string consisting solely of whitespace (e.g., "  ") will pass the existing checks and be saved, violating the requirement.

benchmarkCase.title: Role update regresses last-admin safeguard
benchmarkCase.description: The new role update path can demote the final administrator.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-REGRESS-1: A team must retain at least one administrator; role updates that would demote the final admin must be rejected.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The role update writes the requested role without checking remaining administrators.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: A team can become permanently unmanaged.

expectedFindings.title: Role change can demote the final administrator
expectedFindings.description: The update lacks the required last-admin safety check.

distractors.description: The target membership is checked for existence.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Rejecting an unknown membership is required input handling.

findings.title: Role update allows demoting the final administrator
findings.description: The new code in apps/reference-saas/lib/team-members.ts retrieves a membership, sets member.role = role, and saves it without checking whether this change would remove the team's last administrator. This violates REQ-REGRESS-1, which requires rejecting role updates that would demote the final admin.

benchmarkCase.title: Starter plan seat limit is bypassed
benchmarkCase.description: The invitation flow omits the plan seat check.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-PLAN-2: Starter teams may have at most three active members; over-limit invitations must be rejected.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: An invitation is created without checking active seats against the Starter limit.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Customers can receive paid capacity without upgrading.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation ignores Starter seat limit
expectedFindings.description: The flow sends an invitation without checking the team's active seat count.

distractors.description: The email is checked for an at sign.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Basic email validation is independent of capacity enforcement.

findings.title: Invitations to starter teams not limited to three active members (REQ-PLAN-2)
findings.description: inviteToTeam creates and sends invitations without checking the team's current active member count. REQ-PLAN-2 requires starter teams to have at most three active members and that over-limit invitations be rejected; this function allows invitations to be created/sent regardless of member count.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled trial can be reactivated
benchmarkCase.description: The retry handler treats cancelled subscriptions as recoverable.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-STATE-2: A cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: Every non-active subscription is set to active.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: A user can be restored to a service they explicitly cancelled.

expectedFindings.title: Retry reactivates cancelled trials
expectedFindings.description: The handler changes cancelled trials to active.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Avoiding a redundant write is correct.

findings.title: Cancelled trial can be reactivated by retry
findings.description: The new billing code unconditionally sets subscription.status = "active" (unless already "active") and saves it, without checking for a "cancelled" state. This allows a previously cancelled trial subscription to be reactivated by this code path, violating the requirement that a cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry (REQ-STATE-2).

reviewers.title: Invitations creation endpoint allows any team member to create invites
reviewers.description: The new route grants invite-creation permission to any user who has a membership record in the team. It checks only that a membership exists (findMembership(teamId, user.id)) and returns 403 if not. There is no check that the membership has an administrator role. Therefore non-admin team members can create invitations, violating REQ-AUTH-1 which requires that only team administrators may create invitations.

reviewers.title: Invitation creation allowed for any team member, not just administrators

It checks only that a membership exists and returns 403 if none, but does not verify that the member is an administrator. This permits non-admin members to create invites, violating REQ-AUTH-1: "Only team administrators may create invitations."

reviewers.title: Invite creation allowed for any team member, not restricted to administrators

The patch does not verify the member's role/administrative status before creating the invite, so non-admin members would be able to create invitations — a direct violation of the requirement.

reviewers.title: Queued exports labeled as ready before downloadable file exists
reviewers.description: REQ-UX-3 requires that the dashboard label queued exports as "processing" until a downloadable file exists. The new export-button.tsx immediately shows a success toast "Your export is ready to download" right after issuing the POST to /api/export, without checking whether an export file is available. This presents the export as ready while it may still be queued/processing, violating the requirement.

reviewers.title: Queued exports are labeled as ready before downloadable file exists
reviewers.description: The new exportData function sends a POST to /api/export and immediately shows toast.success("Your export is ready to download") without checking whether a downloadable file is available. REQ-UX-3 requires the dashboard to label queued exports as "processing" until a downloadable file exists. This implementation violates that requirement by presenting the export as ready while it may still be queued or processing on the server.

reviewers.title: Retrying payment does not reuse original idempotency key
reviewers.description: The code creates a new idempotency key with crypto.randomUUID() when charging an invoice. REQ-RETRY-1 requires that retrying a failed payment reuse the original idempotency key; generating a new random key violates this requirement.

reviewers.title: Retrying failed payment generates a new idempotency key instead of reusing original

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event for manual invoice void
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id. The new route implementation voids the invoice but contains no code to record an audit event (no call to an audit/logger API, no creation of an audit record, and no immutable storage of actor and invoice id). This is an explicit violation of REQ-AUDIT-1.

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event when voiding invoice
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void records an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id. The new route handler calls voidInvoice(...) and returns the invoice but contains no code that records an audit event (no call to an audit logging function, no creation of an audit record, and no immutable persistence of actor and invoice id). Therefore the change violates REQ-AUDIT-1.

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event when voiding invoice

reviewers.title: Missing immutable audit event for manual invoice void
reviewers.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id. reviewers.title: Display name length check uses string length including whitespace instead of counting non-whitespace characters
reviewers.description: REQ-VALID-1 requires a display name to contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters. The new route only checks displayName.length (total characters) and does not trim or count non-whitespace characters, so names with fewer than 2 non-whitespace characters (e.g., "  a", " a ", or "  ") could pass, and names with many whitespace characters could be miscounted.

reviewers.title: Display name validation allows whitespace-only names
reviewers.description: REQ-VALID-1 requires a display name to contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters. The added code only checks that displayName is a string and that its length (number of characters) is between 2 and 80. It does not ensure the name contains at least 2 non-whitespace characters — a string of two or more whitespace characters (e.g., "  ") would pass the existing checks but violate the requirement.

reviewers.title: Display name length check counts total characters instead of non-whitespace characters
reviewers.description: REQ-VALID-1 requires a display name to contain 2–80 non-whitespace characters. The new code only verifies typeof displayName === "string" and that displayName.length is between 2 and 80, which counts all characters including whitespace. Therefore inputs with fewer than two non-whitespace characters (for example, "  a", " a ", or "   ") can pass the check even though they don't meet the requirement. Validation should count non-whitespace characters (e.g., by removing whitespace or matching \S) or otherwise ensure at least two non-whitespace characters are present.

reviewers.title: Starter-team invite does not enforce max-active-members limit (REQ-PLAN-2)
reviewers.description: The new inviteToTeam function creates and sends invitations without checking the team type or current active member count. REQ-PLAN-2 requires that starter teams have at most three active members and that invitations exceeding this limit be rejected. The patch lacks any logic to (a) determine whether the team is a starter team, and (b) count active members and reject invitations when the limit would be exceeded. As written, an invitation for a starter team could be created and sent even if the team already has three active members, violating the requirement.

reviewers.title: Cancelled subscription can be reactivated by retry
reviewers.description: The patch unconditionally sets subscription.status = "active" whenever a subscription exists and is not already "active". There is no check preventing transitions from a cancelled state back to active. This violates REQ-STATE-2 which requires that a cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry.

reviewers.title: Cancelled trial can be reactivated by retry
reviewers.description: Code forcefully sets subscription.status = "active" and saves it regardless of prior status, after only checking for an existing subscription and returning early for status "active". There is no check preventing reactivation of subscriptions with status "cancelled" or similar; thus a cancelled trial could be reactivated by this path, violating REQ-STATE-2 (A cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated by retry).

benchmarkCase.title: Member can create team invitations
benchmarkCase.description: Membership is checked but the administrator role is omitted.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUTH-1: Only team administrators may create invitations.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The POST route permits any team member to create an invitation.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Regular members can expand a team without authorization.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation creation does not require an administrator
expectedFindings.description: A regular member can create an invitation because membership is checked without validating the admin role.

distractors.description: The route uses a generic unauthorized error.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: A non-enumerating error message is intentional.

findings.title: Invitations creation endpoint allows non-admin team members to create invites
findings.description: The new route checks only for existence of a membership via findMembership(teamId, user.id) and returns 403 if none. It does not verify that the membership has an administrator role before calling createInvite, allowing any team member (not just administrators) to create invitations, which violates REQ-AUTH-1.

benchmarkCase.title: Export shows success before data is ready
benchmarkCase.description: The UI reports a queued export as downloadable.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-UX-3: The dashboard must label queued exports as processing until a downloadable file exists.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A success toast appears immediately after queueing the job.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Users waste time looking for a file that does not exist.

expectedFindings.title: Queued export is presented as ready
expectedFindings.description: The toast promises a download before the queued job produces it.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Asynchronous processing is allowed when the UI describes it correctly.

findings.title: Queued exports labeled as ready before downloadable file exists
findings.description: The new exportData function posts to /api/export and immediately shows toast.success("Your export is ready to download") without verifying a downloadable file exists or that the export job completed. This violates REQ-UX-3 which requires queued exports be labeled as processing until a downloadable file exists—displaying a ready/downloadable message prematurely can mislead users if the export remains queued or is still being generated.

benchmarkCase.title: Payment retry loses idempotency key
benchmarkCase.description: A retry generates a new charge identity.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-RETRY-1: Retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The retry creates a random key for every charge.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: One invoice can be charged more than once.

expectedFindings.title: Payment retry generates a new idempotency key
expectedFindings.description: A fresh key permits a duplicate charge for the invoice.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The retry cannot charge a non-existent invoice.

findings.title: Retrying payment does not reuse original idempotency key
findings.description: The patch always generates a new idempotency key with crypto.randomUUID() when calling charge(), rather than reusing the original idempotency key for retries. This violates REQ-RETRY-1 which requires that a retry of a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.

findings.title: Missing immutable audit event for manual invoice void
findings.description: REQ-AUDIT-1 requires that every manual invoice void record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id. The new route handler (apps/reference-saas/app/api/invoices/[invoiceId]/void/route.ts) obtains the current user and calls voidInvoice(params.invoiceId, actor.id) but contains no observable call to create or persist an immutable audit record (no audit/log API call, event store write, or explicit audit record creation). No audit is returned in the response either. As written, the change does not satisfy REQ-AUDIT-1.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled notifications are retried
benchmarkCase.description: The retry worker treats cancelled notifications as eligible.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-3: Cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The guard excludes sent notifications but not cancelled ones.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Cancelled messages can reach recipients after cancellation.

expectedFindings.title: Cancelled notifications are eligible for retry
expectedFindings.description: The guard allows cancelled messages to be delivered.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Tracking pending attempts is expected.

findings.title: Cancelled notification may be retried/delivered
findings.description: The patch fetches a notification and only skips sending when notification.status === "sent". It increments attempts and calls send(notification) for any existing notification whose status is not "sent". There is no check to prevent action when notification.status === "cancelled" (or an equivalent cancelled state), so cancelled notifications could be retried or delivered. This behavior violates REQ-NOTIFY-3: "Cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried."

findings.title: Starter-team invite does not enforce max-active-members limit (REQ-PLAN-2)

findings.description: The patch unconditionally sets subscription.status = "active" for any existing subscription that is not already "active". reviewers.title: Queued exports labeled as processing requirement violated
reviewers.description: REQ-UX-3 requires that the dashboard label queued exports as "processing" until a downloadable file exists. The provided patch sends a POST to "/api/export" and unconditionally shows toast.success("Your export is ready to download") immediately after the request completes, without verifying whether a downloadable file exists or whether the export is still queued/processing. This causes the UI to label queued (not-yet-downloadable) exports as ready instead of "processing", violating REQ-UX-3.

reviewers.description: Code creates a new idempotency key using crypto.randomUUID() when charging for an invoice instead of reusing the original idempotency key. This violates REQ-RETRY-1 which requires that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.

reviewers.title: Retry attempted on cancelled notification
reviewers.description: Code increments attempts and calls send() regardless of notification status; it checks only for status === "sent" but does not prevent retries for notifications with status "cancelled". This violates REQ-NOTIFY-3 which mandates that cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.

reviewers.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried/delivered
reviewers.description: Code increments attempts and calls send(notification) for any notification that exists, without checking for a 'cancelled' status. REQ-NOTIFY-3 mandates that cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried. This implementation will allow cancelled notifications to be retried or delivered if their status is not 'sent'.

reviewers.title: Display name validation allows whitespace-only strings

reviewers.title: Starter-team invitation over limit not rejected (REQ-PLAN-2 violation)
reviewers.description: The new inviteToTeam function creates and sends an invitation without checking the current number of active team members. The product requirement REQ-PLAN-2 mandates starter teams may have at most three active members and that invitations exceeding this limit must be rejected. The patch calls getTeam and validates the email but does not fetch or evaluate the team's active member count or enforce the three-member cap before createInvitation/sendEmail.

reviewers.title: Invitations allow exceeding starter team member limit

The new inviteToTeam function does not check the team's current active member count or enforce the three-member limit before creating an invitation. It unconditionally creates and sends an invitation after basic validations, which can permit over-limit invitations for starter teams.

reviewers.title: Does not enforce starter-team member limit when creating invitations

It simply fetches the team, validates the email, creates an invitation, and sends email—allowing invitations that could push a starter team over the three-member limit.

reviewers.title: Cancelled subscription can be reactivated by retry

This allows a previously cancelled trial/subscription to be reactivated by this code path, violating REQ-STATE-2 which mandates that a cancelled trial remains cancelled and may not be reactivated.

benchmarkCase.title: Member can create team invitations
benchmarkCase.description: Membership is checked but the administrator role is omitted.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUTH-1: Only team administrators may create invitations.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The POST route permits any team member to create an invitation.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Regular members can expand a team without authorization.

expectedFindings.title: Invitation creation does not require an administrator
expectedFindings.description: A regular member can create an invitation because membership is checked without validating the admin role.

distractors.description: The route uses a generic unauthorized error.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: A non-enumerating error message is intentional.

findings.title: Invitation creation does not restrict to team administrators
findings.description: The route allows any user who has a membership record on the team to create an invite. The code only checks for membership existence (if (!membership) return 403) and does not verify the membership's role or administrative privilege before calling createInvite. This permits non-administrative members to create invitations, violating REQ-AUTH-1 which requires that only team administrators may create invitations.

benchmarkCase.title: Export shows success before data is ready
benchmarkCase.description: The UI reports a queued export as downloadable.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-UX-3: The dashboard must label queued exports as processing until a downloadable file exists.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A success toast appears immediately after queueing the job.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Users waste time looking for a file that does not exist.

expectedFindings.title: Queued export is presented as ready
expectedFindings.description: The toast promises a download before the queued job produces it.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Asynchronous processing is allowed when the UI describes it correctly.

findings.title: Queued exports labeled as processing requirement violated
findings.description: REQ-UX-3 requires that queued exports be labeled as "processing" until a downloadable file exists. The patch implementation sends a POST to "/api/export" and immediately calls toast.success("Your export is ready to download") after the request completes, without checking for the existence of a downloadable file or verifying that the export has finished processing. This causes the UI to report exports as ready prematurely, violating REQ-UX-3.

benchmarkCase.title: Payment retry loses idempotency key
benchmarkCase.description: A retry generates a new charge identity.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-RETRY-1: Retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The retry creates a random key for every charge.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: One invoice can be charged more than once.

expectedFindings.title: Payment retry generates a new idempotency key
expectedFindings.description: A fresh key permits a duplicate charge for the invoice.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The retry cannot charge a non-existent invoice.

findings.title: Retry does not reuse original idempotency key (REQ-RETRY-1 violation)
findings.description: The patched code always generates a new idempotency key via crypto.randomUUID() when calling charge(), rather than reusing the original idempotency key for a retry. This behavior violates REQ-RETRY-1 which mandates that retrying a failed payment must reuse the original idempotency key.

benchmarkCase.title: Manual invoice void omits audit event
benchmarkCase.description: A required product audit trail is not recorded.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-AUDIT-1: Every manual invoice void must record an immutable audit event with the actor and invoice id.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The endpoint voids the invoice but does not write the audit event.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Support and finance cannot determine who voided an invoice.

expectedFindings.title: Manual invoice void has no audit event
expectedFindings.description: The mutation completes without recording the required actor and invoice audit trail.

distractors.description: The response returns the voided invoice.
distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Returning the updated resource is normal API behavior.

findings.title: Missing immutable audit event on manual invoice void
findings.description: The added route handler calls voidInvoice(params.invoiceId, actor.id) and returns the invoice but does not itself record an immutable audit event containing the actor and invoice id. The patch contains no explicit audit log write, audit-table insert, or event emission. The requirement REQ-AUDIT-1 mandates that every manual invoice void record such an immutable audit event. Unless voidInvoice (not shown in this patch) internally guarantees creation and persistence of the required immutable audit event, this change constitutes a violation of REQ-AUDIT-1.

benchmarkCase.title: Cancelled notifications are retried
benchmarkCase.description: The retry worker treats cancelled notifications as eligible.
benchmarkCase.requirement: REQ-NOTIFY-3: Cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.
benchmarkCase.seededViolation: The guard excludes sent notifications but not cancelled ones.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: Cancelled messages can reach recipients after cancellation.

expectedFindings.title: Cancelled notifications are eligible for retry
expectedFindings.description: The guard allows cancelled messages to be delivered.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: Tracking pending attempts is expected.

findings.title: Cancelled notifications may be retried/delivered
findings.description: The patch only prevents sending when notification.status === "sent". It increments attempts and calls send(notification) for all other statuses, including "cancelled". This allows cancelled notifications to be retried or delivered, violating REQ-NOTIFY-3 which mandates cancelled notifications must never be delivered or retried; only pending notifications may be retried.

benchmarkCase.title: Opted-out users receive billing notices

benchmarkCase.seededViolation: A billing reminder is sent without reading the opt-out preference.
benchmarkCase.whyItMatters: The product disregards a user's communication choice.

expectedFindings.title: Billing reminder ignores opt-out preference
expectedFindings.description: The sender delivers a non-essential reminder without a preference check.

distractors.reasonNotAnIssue: The sender must not send to a missing user.

findings.title: Sends billing reminders without checking user opt-out
findings.description: The new reminders.ts retrieves a user, builds a reminder message, and calls sendEmail(user.email, message) with no check of the user's opt-out or notification preferences. Per REQ-NOTIFY-4, users who have opted out of non-essential billing reminders must not receive them; the code as added can send such reminders to opted-out users.
